$comment: Developer Harness V3 (D3.2) persistent task lifecycle CONTRACT. Design plus a pure reducer (scripts/developer-harness-v3/lifecycle/lifecycle.mjs). There is no runtime, database or scheduler in D3.2. A completed Claude session is NOT a completed task.
recoverable_entry_from: any non-terminal state; the state left is recorded as resume_to and is the only legal exit target (blocked additionally requires an owner action recorded as evidence in a later phase)
completion_rule: completed is reachable only from production_verification, or from merged when acceptance.production_required is false. A session_completed event never changes state.

sequence: detect utilization at or above the threshold using official supported telemetry only
stop starting new work and finish or safely abandon the current step at a safe execution boundary
write a durable checkpoint (task requirements, plan, remaining work, base/head SHAs, worktree snapshot, evidence references) BEFORE ending the session
start a FRESH Claude session from an optimized context pack plus the restored original requirements and remaining-work list
verify the restored state against the checkpoint, then continue automatically with no owner prompt
context_renewal.telemetry: only officially supported, documented sources; verified empirically in D3.3 before use
context_renewal.fallback_when_exact_utilization_unavaila: a conservative, supported proxy chosen in D3.4 (for example renewing at a lower proxy threshold or at step boundaries after a bounded amount of work); never a guess presented as a measurement
forbidden: blind /clear or any context reset that is not preceded by a verified durable checkpoint
renewal that drops or rewrites the original requirements
renewal that requires another owner prompt
context_renewal.state: waiting state context_recovery with reason CONTEXT_RENEWAL; resume_to is the state left; CONTEXT_RENEWAL is never a genuine blocker

recovery_requirements: A task is reconstructable from persisted events, the context pack reference, the base and head SHAs, and the worktree, without Claude session history.
Committed work is recovered from the branch; uncommitted work is recovered from a task-owned worktree snapshot taken at every checkpoint.
Every mutation carries expected_revision, a fencing token and an idempotency id; stale or duplicate mutations are rejected or no-ops.
